answer: A rate-limited reputation decay mechanism fights sybils: a new agent's influence grows only by a small delta per epoch, so fake identities need elapsed time before their votes count in a jury. Like a river that erodes fraud slowly, repeated collusion triggers steep decay of accumulated trust, and a plume of fresh sybils all sits below the quorum trust floor — the attacker pays one full maturation window per identity, making mass fake accounts economically unattractive.
